1.why: Every MFA endpoint uses authenticated() and binds actions only to auth.account from the session; foreign identity fields in the body are rejected.

2.why: Authenticator checks compare against the global TEST_AUTHENTICATOR_CODE rather than a per-user TOTP, so the same code would validate for any account.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/confirm updates account.mfa but does not invalidate or rotate any other existing sessions in the sessions Map.

4.why: The OTP secret is stored with AES-GCM encryptSecret and recovery codes are stored only as SHA-256 hashes via storeRecoveryCodes.

5.why: Secrets, session IDs, CSRF tokens, and recovery codes are produced with crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: The session cookie is HttpOnly and the client keeps secrets/codes only in in-memory JS variables, not localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validators (isEmail, isPhone, isOtp, isRecovery, isSecret) gate inputs and bodies are size-limited and type-checked.

8.why: Dynamic values are written with textContent/escText; user input is not interpolated into HTML as markup.

10.why: securityHeaders sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, and related hardening headers on responses.

11.why: cookie() sets mfa_session with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Server errors are generic without stack traces, but secrets, test OTPs, and recovery codes are returned to the client and written to the on-page/console logs panel.

13.why: Identity, enrollment, and MFA challenges set used=true after success and enforce expires (CHALLENGE_MS); recovery codes are consumed permanently.

14.why: failed() increments failures and locks for LOCK_MS after five bad attempts on identity, enrollment, challenge, and recovery guards.

15.why: rotateAuthenticated issues a new session id after identity verify, idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in sessionFrom, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
